citations.quote:
Let $T$ be a compact torus and $M$ a compact smooth manifold without boundary. A smooth left $T$-action is a jointly smooth map $a:T\times M\to M$ with $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(st,x)=a(s,a(t,x))$. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank complex vector bundles on $M$. For each $j<N$, let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be a linear differential operator of finite order, and put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$. The sequence is a complex when $d_{j+1}d_j=0$ for every $j$. It is **elliptic** when, for every $x\in M$ and every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi\in T_x^*M$, the sequence of principal-symbol maps

$$0\longrightarrow E_x^0\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_0)(x,\xi)}E_x^1\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_1)(x,\xi)}\cdots\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_{N-1})(x,\xi)}E_x^N\longrightarrow0$$

is exact. Suppose each bundle has a smooth $T$-linearization $\rho_t^j:E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$, satisfying the group-action law, and the induced section maps

$$ (U_t^j s)(x):=\rho_t^j\bigl(s(t^{-1}\cdot x)\bigr) $$

commute with $d_j$. Require the cohomology spaces $H^j(E^\bullet):=\ker d_j/\operatorname{im}d_{j-1}$ to be finite-dimensional. The representation ring $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional continuous complex representations of $T$. Define

$$\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j[H^j(E^\bullet)]\in R(T),\qquad \chi_{E^\bullet}(t):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}\!\left(U_t^j\bigm|_{H^j(E^\bullet)}\right).$$

For a two-term complex $0\to C^\infty(M,E^+)\xrightarrow{D^+}C^\infty(M,E^-)\to0$, this gives $[\ker D^+]-[\operatorname{coker}D^+]$. This definition concerns elliptic complexes, not transversally elliptic operators.

Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, $n=\dim M>0$, and $E$ a finite-rank Hermitian bundle. Let $P$ be a smooth second-order differential operator with positive-frequency principal symbol $p(x,\xi)$, a Hermitian matrix satisfying $p(x,\xi)\ge c|\xi|^2I$ for some $c>0$. Assume its nonnegative selfadjoint realization has a complete orthonormal basis of smooth eigensections and a smooth heat kernel $K_t(y,z):E_z\to E_y$ relative to Riemannian volume. No scalar-principal-symbol hypothesis is imposed. In normal coordinates and smooth unitary frames based at $x$, set

$$k_x(w)=(2\pi)^{-n}\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{iw\cdot\xi}e^{-p(x,\xi)}\,d\xi.$$

Then $k_x$ is Schwartz, $\int k_x(w)\,dw=I$, and, locally uniformly for bounded $a,b\in T_xM$,

$$t^{n/2}K_t(\exp_x(\sqrt t\,a),\exp_x(\sqrt t\,b))\longrightarrow k_x(a-b).$$

For every integer $L>n$ there is $C_L$ such that

$$\|K_t(y,z)\|\le C_Lt^{-n/2}(1+d(y,z)/\sqrt t)^{-L}\qquad(0<t\le1).$$

In dimension zero the corresponding assertion is the finite-dimensional limit $K_t(x,x)\to I$ and zero kernel between distinct points.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly by isometries on a compact Riemannian manifold $M$ without boundary. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank Hermitian bundles and, for $0\le j<N$, let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be first-order differential maps with $d_{j+1}d_j=0$. Assume the principal-symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero real cotangent vector. Suppose smooth unitary bundle maps $\rho_t^j:E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$ satisfy $\rho_e^j=I$ and $\rho_{st}^j|_{E_x^j}=\rho_s^j|_{E_{t\cdot x}^j}\circ\rho_t^j|_{E_x^j}$, and commute with all $d_j$; on sections set $(U_t^j s)(y)=\rho_t^j(s(t^{-1}\cdot y))$. Put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$, $E^{\mathrm{ev}}=\bigoplus_{j\text{ even}}E^j$, $E^{\mathrm{odd}}=\bigoplus_{j\text{ odd}}E^j$, $d=\bigoplus_jd_j$, and $\Delta=(d+d^*)^2$, where $d^*$ is the formal adjoint for the chosen metrics and Riemannian volume. For the nonnegative selfadjoint Hodge realization on $L^2$, assume that $\Delta$ has discrete spectrum, smooth eigensections, a trace-class heat operator $e^{-t\Delta}$ with smooth kernel for every $t>0$, finite-dimensional cohomology, and a harmonic representative for each cohomology class. For $g\in T$, let $M^g=\{x\in M:g\cdot x=x\}$, and suppose each $x\in M^g$ is simple, meaning $I-dg_x:T_xM\to T_xM$ is invertible. Then

$$\lim_{t\downarrow0}\operatorname{Str}(U_g e^{-t\Delta})=\sum_{x\in M^g}\frac{\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}(\rho_g^j|_{E_x^j})}{|\det_{\mathbb R}(I-dg_x)|}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Str}$ is the trace on $E^{\mathrm{ev}}$ minus the trace on $E^{\mathrm{odd}}$. The simplicity condition makes $M^g$ a finite set; the determinant is the normal Jacobian at that isolated fixed point.

Assume countable choice. The negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform is continuous $\mathcal F:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$, and
$$\mathcal F(\partial^\alpha f)(\xi)=(2\pi i\xi)^\alpha\widehat f(\xi),\qquad \partial^\beta\widehat f=\mathcal F((-2\pi ix)^\beta f).$$

Assume countable choice. For every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$ and every $x\in\mathbb R^n$,
$$f(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\widehat f(\xi)e^{2\pi ix\cdot\xi}\,d\xi.$$
The integral is absolutely convergent.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B,\nu)$ be sigma-finite measure
spaces, and let $f : X \times Y \to \mathbb C$ belong to
$L^1(\mu \times \nu)$. Then:

1. for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the section $f_x$ belongs to $L^1(\nu)$;
2. for $\nu$-almost every $y$, the section $f^y$ belongs to $L^1(\mu)$;
3. after assigning the value $0$ on the exceptional parameter sets, the
   section-integral functions are integrable; and
4. the three integrals agree:
$$\int_{X \times Y} f\,d(\mu \times \nu) = \int_X \left(\int_Y f_x\,d\nu\right)d\mu = \int_Y \left(\int_X f^y\,d\mu\right)d\nu.$$

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$
